Loudong: The Lay Practitioner Shenglian Luo Wanzhong (Yunmei) has sponsored the printing of *A Brief Account of Encouraging Rebirth*.
That which lacks evidence and proof is not worthy of belief; that which possesses corroboration and verification is its teaching.
It is certain and true that those who practice mindfulness of the Buddha and attain rebirth in the Pure Land do so with manifest evidence and verification.
For while all matters in the world may be subject to deception or pretense, the matter of life and death alone cannot be feigned in the slightest degree.

Throughout antiquity and the present, the sages, worthies, heroes, and men of talent who have expounded the Way, discussed virtue, cultivated benevolence, and practiced righteousness have numbered in the tens of thousands, even millions; yet when they passed away, [their accounts] were not...
To pass away while lying ill upon a bed is considered a natural end to one's life. However, if one wishes to know in advance that the time has come, they should bathe and sit upright.
Then, either a wondrous fragrance will fill the room, or celestial music will arise spontaneously in the sky.

Since the beginning of human civilization, there has never been a single person who experienced this, with the sole exception of those who practice the recitation of the Buddha’s name (*nienfo*). Such auspicious signs are not limited to these alone.
It is sufficient. One should neither begrudge nor hold in high esteem those who practice the recitation of the Buddha’s name.
Since one is so peaceful and at ease at the moment of departure, the place one reaches will surely be an extraordinary land of merit.
How can people fail to give rise to a single thought of resolve at this very moment? For this reason, I shall take this place...

I have selected several dozen passages from those who were born in the Western Paradise and titled this work "A Brief Account of Rebirth. My intention is that those who behold these examples may reflect upon them with a desire for self-improvement, so that we may all together be reborn in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing. Thus it is said.
Regarding the category of Bodhisattvas who attain rebirth and receive the prediction of becoming a Tathāgata,
the *Mahā-amitāyur-dhyāna-sūtra* states: Maitreya addressed the Buddha, saying, "In this world, how many Bodhisattvas go [to that land]?"
They will be born in Sukhāvatī. The Buddha told Maitreya: "In this world, there are sixty-two billion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas who will be reborn in that land;

the number of bodhisattvas of minor practice is beyond calculation. Not only from this land, but also from other buddha-fields—such as the realm of the Buddha Dūriprabha—there are eighteen billion bodhisattvas who shall all be reborn there, and so on throughout the ten directions."
In that Buddha-field, those who attain rebirth are exceedingly numerous and beyond counting; were I to describe them in detail, even an entire eon would not suffice.
In the *Mañjuśrīpraṇidhāna-jātismaraṇa-buddhasamādhi-sūtra*, the Buddha prophesied that Mañjuśrī would be born in Sukhāvatī. The verse of aspiration uttered by Mañjuśrī says: "May..."
When my life comes to an end, may all obstacles be extinguished; may I behold Amitābha Buddha face-to-face and be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Having been born in that Buddha-land, may I fulfill my great vows; may the Tathāgata Amitābha appear before me and bestow upon me the prophecy of enlightenment.

In the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Samantabhadra seeks rebirth [in the Pure Land]. The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra sets forth ten kinds of great vows, universally seeking rebirth in the Pure Land for the sake of all sentient beings.
A verse says: "May I, when my life is about to end, completely eliminate all obstacles and behold that Buddha face-to-face."
"Amitābha! One shall immediately attain rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

Regarding the verse treatise on the Pure Land by the Bodhisattva Maitreya (Tianqin): he was a person from India who extensively composed various treatises; he ascended to the Inner Court of the Tuṣita Heaven palace and beheld Amitābha.

Le Fu composed the *Commentary on the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life* (*Wǔliàngshòu jīng lùn*) and the *Verses on the Pure Land* (*Jìngtǔ jì*). He propagated the Five-Gate Method of Practice (*Wǔmén xiūfǎ*) and universally exhorted others to be reborn [in the Pure Land].

He invited a Bodhisattva with the five supernatural powers from the Kukkutārāma Monastery in India to travel by means of his spiritual power to the Land of Peace and Bliss (*Anlè guó*). There, he beheld Amitābha...
Buddha. Chen said, "The sentient beings of this Sahā world wish to be reborn in the Pure Land, yet they lack the physical form and demeanor of the Buddha;

I pray that you deign to descend. The Buddha said, "You should first go ahead; I shall soon appear there. After he had returned with his five supernatural powers (*pañcābhijñā*), the sacred image had already arrived:

one Buddha and fifty bodhisattvas, each seated upon a lotus flower atop a tree leaf. Subsequently, it was copied and circulated; this is recorded in the *Gantong zhuan* (Biographies of Spiritual Resonance).
Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa, the twelfth patriarch of the Western Heavens, composed the *Awakening of Faith*. Later, he clarified the aspiration for rebirth in the Pure Land;
his words are all concise and essential.
The *Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra*,
in the section on Nāgārjuna’s prophecy, states: "O Mahāmati, you should know that after the Parinirvāṇa of the Sugata, there will be in a future age one who upholds my Dharma—
a bhikṣu of great name and virtue known as Nāgārjuna, who will be able to destroy the tenets of existence and non-existence."

In the interim, he manifested the unsurpassed Mahāyāna Dharma for me, whereby I attained the first stage, the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), and was reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
Regarding the accumulation of merit for rebirth, the *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra* states: The Buddha said, "After my parinirvāṇa, in the country of Northern India, there will be a bhikṣu named Gopa."
Kāśyapa, having cultivated and accumulated immeasurable and diverse roots of goodness for supreme enlightenment, he will pass away and be reborn in the Land of Immeasurable Life,

located beyond hundreds of thousands of billions of worlds to the west. There, in the presence of that Buddha, he will plant various roots of goodness and shall later become a buddha named Vimalaprabhā (Stainless Light).

The *Sūtra on the Birthplace of Bodhisattvas Who Have Attained Patience and Reborn There* states: The Buddha said, "At that time, Makhādeva attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Five hundred laymen and twenty-five laywomen all attained the stage of non-retrogression. When their lives ended, they were all reborn together in the Immeasurable [Life]."
In the Pure Land of the Buddha of Longevity,

the eminent assembly has recorded the name of Chan Master Ze of Changlu. Following the legacy of the Great Master Huiyuan, he established the Lotus Eminent Assembly and universally exhorted [the practice of] mindfulness.
One night, the Buddha dreamed of a youth wearing a black cap and white robes, whose appearance was refined and beautiful. The youth bowed and said, "I wish to enter your Lotus Assembly of Excellence;
I beg you to write down my name. The Master asked what his name was, and he replied, "Puhui (Universal Wisdom).

Having written it down, the youth added, "My elder brother Puxian (Universal Good) also begs that you write his name as well. Upon waking, the Master marveled at this and suddenly recalled the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*’s chapter on "Detachment from the World."
In the "Chapter on the Intervals," there are two Bodhisattvas named Samantabhadra and Samantamukha, who respectively pose two hundred questions and provide two thousand answers in succession.
These are great Bodhisattvas; how could they possibly receive such profound spiritual empowerment? Consequently, I have inscribed these two Bodhisattvas as the presiding deities of this assembly.
Master Tiantai said: "When ordinary monks form a religious society and ancient sages inscribe their names therein, how profound this is! It shows that the Pure Land is no small matter.
This is truly because when an undertaking arises from sincere heart, there is a subtle communion with spiritual response; it cannot be forced to occur."
Section on the Rebirth of Eminent Monks:
Grand Master Huiyuan of the Jin Dynasty.
Huiyuan was a native of Loulan in Yanmen. He was widely versed in secular classics and was particularly proficient in the Six Classics. Having heard of Dharma Master Daoan...
While lecturing on the *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, he attained a sudden and great awakening. Consequently, he shaved his head and received the precepts.

In the sixth year of the Taiyuan era, he passed through Xunyang and saw that Mount Lu was secluded and spacious, a place where one could set the mind at rest. Thereupon, he was moved by a mountain deity who appeared in a dream;

one night, amidst thunder and rain, timber arrived of its own accord. The Regional Inspector, Huan Yi, then constructed a hall for him, naming it "Divinely Transported" (*Shenyun*), as Huiyong had previously resided there.

Xilin (Suxi) thus named his residence Donglin (East Grove). He established a Nianfo Society and did not enter the secular world for thirty years, dedicating himself exclusively to the Western Pure Land.
He fashioned a six-period lotus water-clock and never ceased his recitations. One hundred and forty eminent monks and great scholars joined the society;
concentrating their minds and fixing their thoughts, they beheld the sacred countenance three times, yet he remained grave and silent. Ten years later...
On the evening of the last day of the seventh month in the ninth year, while at the Prajñā Terrace, he was just arising from meditative concentration when he beheld Amitābha Buddha.
His body filled the void of space, and within his circular halo were immeasurable transformation Buddhas, with Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta standing in attendance on his left and right.
He also saw flowing water radiating light, divided into fourteen streams, swirling upward and downward as they proclaimed the wondrous Dharma. The Buddha said: "I..."
"By the power of my original vows, I have come to comfort you. Seven days from now, you shall be born in my land.
He further saw Buddhasena, Huichi, Huiyong, Liu Yimin, and others who had already attained rebirth there, all standing by the Buddha's side. The Master was filled with joy.

He said to his disciples, "Since I first resided here, I have already witnessed the manifestation of the holy form three times; now I behold it once more. I shall certainly be reborn in the Pure Land.
When the appointed time arrived, he sat upright and passed away. This was the sixth day of the eighth month in the twelfth year of the Yixi era.
Huiyong (Jìn Huiyong) was a native of Henei. He entered the monastic order at the age of twelve. Subsequently, he and Master Huiyuan both relied upon Dharma Master Dao’an.
At the beginning of the Taiyuan era, he took up residence on Mount Lu. The Regional Inspector, Tao Fan, donated his own residence to establish Xilin Monastery for him to dwell in.

He severed his will from worldly clamor and set his mind upon the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (Sukhāvatī). In the tenth year of the Yixi era, he manifested his passing; suddenly, he adjusted his robes and attempted to rise.

Startled, the assembly asked him why, and he replied, "The Buddha has come to welcome me. Having finished speaking, he passed away. A wondrous fragrance lingered for seven days before it finally vanished.
Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang dynasty posthumously conferred upon him the title of Great Master Juejizhao.

Sengrui (352–436) was a monk of the Jin dynasty from Jizhou. Having traveled to study in various regions and journeyed as far as India, he returned to Guanzhong, where he received the teachings on the meaning of the sutras from Master Kumārajīva.

Later, he joined the Lotus Society at Mount Lu, where he devoted himself single-mindedly to the practice of *nianfo* (Buddha-recollection). This was the sixteenth year of the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
In his final year, he suddenly announced to the assembly, "I am about to depart. Facing west with palms joined, he passed away.
The assembly saw a golden lotus flower before the Master’s couch that vanished in an instant, while five-colored fragrant smoke issued forth from his room.

Daojing of the Jin dynasty. A native of Langye, his grandfather was Wang Ningzhi, who served as the Regional Inspector of Jiangzhou. Daojing subsequently followed Master Huiyuan to enter the monastic order.

At the age of seventeen, he was widely versed in the sutras and treatises, memorizing ten thousand words a day. He maintained a steadfast faith in the Buddha, never ceasing his practice from dawn until night. During the Yongchu era...
In the first year, he addressed the assembly, saying, "The former master has given me his command; it is time for me to depart. He sat upright, recollecting the Buddha, and passed away.
The assembly saw a radiance fill the room, which did not vanish until a long time had passed.
Sengxian (fl.

Jin dynasty), whose secular name was Zhu Sengxian, traveled south to the region east of the Yangtze River. There he fell ill; he focused his mind exclusively on the Western Land [of Ultimate Bliss], practicing with such earnest devotion that it never faltered.
Suddenly, he saw Amitābha Buddha’s light illuminating his own body, and all his ailments were healed. He immediately rose to bathe and recounted this experience to those around him.
He recounted what he had seen and set forth exhortations on cause and effect; his words were earnest and poignant. At dawn, he sat upright and passed away.
Zhìtōng (石晉) was a native of Fēngxiáng. Having encountered the *Jìngtǔ Yíshì* (Rituals for the Pure Land) by Master Zhìzhě, he could not contain his joy.
He was filled with joy. From then on, he never spat toward the west nor sat with his back to the west, but devoted himself single-mindedly to the recitation of the Buddha’s name.

Later, he saw white cranes and peacocks flying in formation toward the west; he also saw lotus flowers opening and closing before him. He then said, "The white cranes and peacocks are the scenery of the Pure Land;
the radiant appearance of the lotus flowers is the place where one is reborn. The Pure Land has appeared! Thereupon, he rose to prostrate before the Buddha.
[The biography] ends. At the time of his cremation, auspicious clouds of five colors encircled and covered the flames. His *śarīra* were arranged like scales upon his body.
[His disciple] Hui-guang resided in Luoyang and composed commentaries on the *Avataṃsaka*, the *Nirvāṇa*, and the *Daśabhūmika*. One day, while he was ill, he saw...
The celestial hosts came to welcome her. Huiguang said, "My vow is to be reborn only in the Pure Land. She then focused her mind exclusively on the Buddha of Recollection.

Shortly thereafter, she saw a transformation Buddha coming through the air to meet her. Huiguang prostrated and said, "I pray that you will receive me. Just as her prayer was finished, the Buddha vanished.

Daozhen of the Liang dynasty resided at Mount Lu and cultivated the practice of purity. He once dreamed that he was on a boat in the sea heading west; when he asked where they were going, the voice replied, "We are going to the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Daozhen requested to go along with them, but the voice from within the boat said, "You have not yet prepared a bathhouse, nor have you recited the name of Amitābha."
The monk was unable to proceed. He would wake at dawn to bathe the monks and recite the sutras, continuing this for years without ceasing.
Later, he saw a silver platform descend upon the surface of the pond; Zhen silently noted this auspicious omen and kept it secret, saying nothing.

One night, the local people saw a thousand torches of blazing fire on the mountainside, reflecting and illuminating one another, and they said it was various kings coming to pay their respects. When they went to investigate at dawn, they realized it was Zhen.
He had already passed away through transformation.

Shenluan (later known as Tanluan) of the Later Wei dynasty traveled to Mount Wutai in his youth; moved by its spiritual wonders, he left the household life. By nature, he was fond of the pursuit of longevity and cherished the works of Tao [Hongjing].
The Recluse’s Scripture on the Immortals in ten fascicles. Later, he encountered Bodhiruci and asked him, "Does the Buddha possess an art for longevity and immortality?
Bodhiruci smiled and said, "Longevity and immortality are the Way of our Buddha.

He then bestowed upon him the *Sūtra of the Sixteen Contemplations*, saying, "If you study this, then the three realms will not be worth being born into, and the six paths will no longer be visited. As for its duration of life, it is like the flow of a river."

It would be like comparing a single grain of sand to the sands of an eon; nothing could equal it. Sengluan was greatly delighted and subsequently burned the immortal scriptures to devote himself exclusively to the practice of Pure Land Buddhism.
Whether in cold or heat, or during illness and pain, he never slackened even slightly. The Ruler of Wei titled him "Divine Luán. One day, he saw a foreign monk who said to him:

"I am Nāgārjuna. Because you share my same resolve, I have come to meet you. When Sengluan realized that his time had come, he gathered the assembly and exhorted them, saying, "The various sufferings of hell must not be disregarded;
the pure karma of the nine grades must be cultivated. He then commanded his disciples to chant the Buddha’s name aloud.
Facing west and prostrating himself, he passed away. After a long while, the assembly heard the music of the heavens coming from the west.
That was the end.

The Great Master Zhizhe, Zhizhi of the Sui Dynasty, was titled the Great Master Zhizhe. When he was still a child, he would prostrate upon seeing a Buddhist image and invariably bow whenever he encountered a monk. At the age of...

18. He left the household life at Guoyuan Temple. Later, he paid homage to the Great Meditation Master Tanshi of Mount Nanyue and composed the *Commentary on the Guan Wuliangshou Jing*, the *Ten Doubts Treatise*, and other works to extol the Pure Land.
As he was about to pass away, he said to his disciples, "My worldly ties have come to an end."
Having finished chanting the title of the *Sūtra of the Sixteen Contemplations*, he further said: "The Western Pure Land is easy to reach, yet few people go there.

Even those for whom the signs of the 'fire chariot' have appeared can still attain rebirth if they repent for a single thought; how much more so for those who cultivate themselves through the熏習 (*vāsanā*) of precepts and meditative concentration?
Zhilang asked, "I do not know at what stage of realization the Great Master has entered. He replied, "I have merely attained the fifth grade. He added, "As for the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara..."
He came to welcome me. Having finished speaking, he recited the names of the Triple Gem and entered a state like meditative absorption.
Regarding Dharma Master Sui Deng:
while Dharma Master Deng was lecturing on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* at Xingguo Temple in Bingzhou, those who came to listen to the sutra were all universally exhorted [by him].
She attained rebirth in the Pure Land through the practice of mindfulness of the Buddha. She passed away in the twelfth year of the Kaihuang era; a rare fragrance filled her chamber.
At her enshrinement, auspicious clouds and fragrant scents pervaded all the surrounding villages.
The Venerable Shandao was a native of Tang.
During the Zhenguan era, he visited Master Chuo’s Nine Grades Practice Hall in Xihé and said with joy, "This is truly the essential gateway for entering the Buddha-way.
Thereupon, he devoted himself to diligent practice, reciting and chanting day and night; whenever he entered his room, he would kneel in the *hu-gui* posture.

He practiced the recitation of the Buddha’s name with such intensity that he did not cease even when his strength was exhausted; even during the coldest winters, he would sometimes break into a sweat.

After emerging from meditation, he would preach the teachings on the Pure Land to others for over thirty years without ever sleeping. He preferred that food be sent to the kitchen for him, while he himself maintained a frugal and simple diet.

With whatever offerings he received, he had one hundred thousand copies of the *Amitābha Sūtra* transcribed and painted three hundred murals depicting the transformations of the Pure Land, thereby leading many to conversion through his influence.
Those who have done so are very numerous. There are those who have recited the *Amitābha Sūtra* one hundred thousand times, up to five hundred thousand times;

and those who have made it their daily practice to chant the Buddha’s name ten thousand times, up to one hundred thousand times. Those who attained the *nien-fo samādhi* and were reborn in the Western Land are beyond counting.
Their verse at the time of death says: "Gradually the skin becomes like that of a chicken and the hair turns white like a crane; Look, look—our gait has become as feeble as a decrepit old man."
Even if gold and jade fill one’s hall, one cannot avoid the suffering of decay and illness; no matter how many kinds of pleasures you may enjoy, impermanence will inevitably arrive.
There is only the path of direct cultivation: simply recite the name of Amitābha Buddha. One day, he suddenly said to others, "This body is loathsome;
I shall return to the West. He then climbed a willow tree and passed away. Emperor Gaozong learned of this.
The imperial plaque for the temple was bestowed with the name "Guangming" (Luminous).

Dharma Master Kang, whose secular surname was Tang, was a native of Jingyun. At the age of fifteen, he had mastered the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and the *Śūraṅgama-samādhi-sūtra*. During the Zhenyuan era, he visited Baima Temple.
Light radiated from the characters within [the scroll]. Upon examining it, he found it to be the text for the Western Paradise (Xifang) composed by the Venerable Shandao.
He then made this vow: "If I have a karmic affinity with the Pure Land, I pray that you will radiate light once more. Having finished his prayer, the radiance grew even more intense.

He subsequently traveled to the Shadow Hall of the Venerable Shandao in Chang’an to pay his respects; there, he suddenly saw the portrait of the deceased master ascend into the hall. Later, he arrived at Xinding, where he was first converted.
The children recited the Buddha’s name. At first, those who recited it once were given one coin; subsequently, those who could recite it ten times were also given one coin.
After more than a year, everyone—regardless of age or social status—knew how to recite the Buddha’s name.
He then established a Pure Land practice hall at Mount Oryong to encourage his students. On the third day of the tenth month in the twenty-first year thereafter, he gave his final instructions.
The common saying was: "One should give rise to a mind of joyful aspiration for the Pure Land and a mind of weary detachment toward Jambudvīpa.
Thereupon, he emitted several rays of extraordinary light and passed away.
Huaiyu of the Tang dynasty was a native of Taizhou. He wore commoner’s clothes and took but one meal a day; he sat constantly and did not lie down.

He recited the *Amitābha Sūtra* three hundred thousand times and chanted the name of the Buddha fifty thousand times daily. In the first year of the Tiānbǎo era, he beheld sacred images filling the void of space. One—
A person arrived carrying a silver platform. Fayu said, "Throughout my life I have practiced with diligence, vowing to attain a golden platform.

Why is it not so? Thereupon, the silver platform vanished. After twenty-one days, the one who had been carrying the platform appeared again and said, "Because of your diligence, you shall ascend to the highest grade.
You should sit in the lotus posture and wait. Three days later, a wondrous light filled the room. He said to his disciples, "I am reborn..."
He passed away with a smile, having attained the Pure Land. The Prefect of the Commandery, Lord Duan, composed a verse in praise, saying:

"My Master ascended to the First Stage in a single thought; To the music of the celestial harps of the Land of Bliss, he has come twice. Only that ancient locust tree before my gate— Its branches now bend low, merely to support his golden dais."
Daoyang (d. 639) was a native of Wei Commandery. He frequently lectured on the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* and the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*, and exhorted people to seek rebirth in the Western Land.

Later, he foreknew that his time had come and announced his departure for the world in the eighth month; however, people did not believe him. When the first day of the eighth month arrived, [he]... nothing remained.

The Master asked whether the time for the midday meal had arrived. He then ascended the high seat; incense from the burner ignited spontaneously. Leading the fourfold assembly, he recited the Bodhisattva Precepts.

Upon finishing his recitation, he saw a multitude of celestial beings appearing in profusion and the sounds of pipes and strings resounding clearly. He addressed the assembly, saying, "The Tuṣita Heaven is welcoming me.
However, the heavenly realms are the very root of birth and death, not my original aspiration. I originally sought rebirth in the Western Land."
I truly do not know why it did not ultimately succeed. Suddenly, the celestial music vanished;

there was only seen incense, flowers, and musical instruments filling the void from the west, circling above his head. The great assembly looked up, and those far and near were filled with wonder and admiration.

Daowang said, "The signs of the Pure Land have appeared; I shall now depart. Having finished speaking, the incense in his burner suddenly fell from his hand, and he immediately [passed away] upon his high seat.

Huà. Sengxuàn, a monk from the Tang dynasty, was a native of Bingzhou. Initially, he focused his devotion on Maitreya, vowing to be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven. At the age of ninety, he encountered the Way.
Master Chuo heard of the Pure Land and first turned his mind toward the recitation of the Buddha’s name. He prostrated himself a thousand times daily, single-mindedly and without indolence.
Later, when he fell ill, he told his disciples: "Amitābha Buddha has bestowed upon me a fragrant robe; Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta together extend their jeweled hands.
It is time for me to depart. Having finished speaking, he passed away. For seven days, a wondrous fragrance did not dissipate. At that time, there was Qi... [text fragment].
The two Dharma Masters Fangyuan and Guo witnessed these events firsthand; they too aroused a fierce resolve, vowing that they must certainly be reborn in the Western Land.

Day and night, they recited the Buddha’s name without ceasing. Suddenly, they saw the Buddha and the Great Beings (Bodhisattvas) seated upon a jeweled platform by the side of a pond made of the seven treasures.
The two monks prostrated themselves, and the Buddha said: "Those who call my name shall all be born in my land. They further saw three jeweled stairways, one of which was white.
Regarding their robes: one was half lay and half monastic, while the other was exclusively monastic. Both had recited the Buddha’s name with utmost sincerity.
Five days later, those who were to be reborn in that land suddenly heard the sound of a bell, and both monks passed away simultaneously.

Shouhong Tangshouhong was a native of Fenyang. He single-mindedly recited the Buddha’s name, seeking rebirth in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (Sukhāvatī). As he was about to pass away, he saw a youth from Tuṣita Heaven coming to welcome him.
Shouhong said, "I have vowed to go westward; I shall not be born in the heavens. He then immediately led the assembly in reciting the Buddha’s name. Before long—
Ji Hong said, "The Buddha came from the West," and having finished speaking, he passed away.
Daxing of Tang resided at Mount Tai, where he practiced the Samantabhadra Repentance Method for three years. In his later years, he was moved by the manifestation of the Great Being (Mahāsattva).
Upon entering the imperial library to present his petitions, he happened upon a copy of the *Amitābha Sūtra*. He recited and upheld it day and night for twenty-one days.

On the twenty-first day, he beheld the Buddha and the Great Beings (Bodhisattvas) manifesting their forms upon a floor of lapis lazuli. When Emperor Xizong heard of this, he issued an edict summoning him into the palace and bestowed upon him the title "Bodhisattva Constantly Diligent.
One year later, the lapis lazuli floor appeared once more, and he passed away that very day. A wondrous fragrance lingered for ten days, and his flesh [remained intact].
His body did not decay.

Mingzhan of the Tang dynasty—Mingzhan devoted himself to the aspiration for rebirth in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (An-yang) in his later years, never ceasing his recitation of the Buddha’s name. When some mocked him for being late in life, he said:

"If even one who has achieved success through ten recitations can still behold the Buddha, why should I have any anxiety? Later, while ill at Xingjiao Monastery, he prepared a vegetarian feast to bid farewell to both the clergy and the laity;
the Chief Secretaries Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui were both present. After noon had passed, he adjusted his dignified demeanor and recited the Buddha's name.
Suddenly, he said, "The Buddha is coming! The two Great Beings have also arrived. With his body trembling and his palms joined, he passed away.
Chan Master Yongming Shou was a native of Yuhang.
Initially, he served as a clerk in the county treasury. While transporting treasury silver to Xihe, he spent it all to purchase living beings and set them free.
He was destined for death; hearing that he was to be executed, he was greatly overjoyed and said, "Though I die this time, I shall certainly go to the Western Paradise. What I...
He released life, countless tens of millions of times. King Qian Liu specifically issued an edict of amnesty for him to become a monk, bestowing upon him the name Yanshou.
He took ordination under Master Cuoyan of Siming and studied under National Teacher Shaokang of Tiantai, where he realized the essential point of the mind.

Later, he went to Yongming and devoted himself exclusively to the practice of Pure Land. At night, he stayed on a separate peak and led the assembly in reciting the Buddha’s name; those nearby occasionally heard celestial voices.
The music resounded through the air. King Zhongyi sighed and remarked, "Since antiquity, no one has sought the Western Paradise with such single-minded earnestness.

He then constructed the Xiangyan Hall for the Western Paradise to fulfill his aspiration. On the twenty-sixth day of the second month in the eighth year of the Kaibao era, he rose at dawn, burned incense, and addressed the assembly.
He sat in the lotus position and passed away. Later, a monk arrived from Linchuan after having been gone for a year.

He circumambulated the stupa. When people questioned him, he said, "I was ill and entered the underworld. I saw a statue of a monk enshrined to the left of the hall, which the King of the Underworld worshipped morning and evening.
I secretly inquired about this person, and they replied, 'This is Chan Master Yongming Shou of Hangzhou. All who die must pass through this place;
yet this master was reborn directly in the Western Pure Land at the highest level of the upper grade. Because the King esteemed his virtue, [he thus honored him]."
Homage and Respect.

Dharma Master Yuanjing Chang (also known as Song Shengchang) was a native of Qiantang. He entered the monastic order at the age of seven. During the Chunhua era, he resided at Nan Zhaoqing Temple and admired Mount Lu.

Following this tradition, [Zhao] pricked his finger to draw blood and transcribed the "Chapter on Pure Conduct" from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, dedicating the merit toward rebirth in the Western Paradise.
Among the scholar-officials who participated in the assembly, they were designated as "disciples of pure conduct," with the Duke Wenzheng Wang Dan at their head.

At that time, there were one hundred and twenty officials, including dukes, ministers, governors, and regional commanders, along with one thousand bhikṣus. Su Yijian of the Hanlin Academy composed the "Pure Conduct Chapter."
Preface. He said to me: "I would not have declined even if I had had to spread my hair to receive his feet or gouge out my own flesh to request the Dharma;
how much less would I begrudge this humble writing and shallow learning? On the twelfth day of the first month in the fourth year of the Tianxi era, he sat upright reciting the Buddha’s name.
After a short while, he cried out with vigor, "The Buddha has come! and then passed away peacefully.

Jingguan of the Song dynasty resided at Jiguang Hermitage in Jiahe. Having practiced the Pure Land repentance rites for over ten years, he said to his disciples, "In twenty-seven days, I shall depart.
Two days prior to that appointed time, he saw a red lotus flower; on the following day—
Furthermore, he saw yellow lotuses filling the room, upon which a transformed youth sat, his lower body bound with a sash of immortals' grass.
On the third day, he entered the coffin and sat upright, commanding the assembly to recite the Buddha’s name. Shortly thereafter, he passed away.
Ciyun Chanmaster Song Zunshe was a native of Linhai County in Taizhou. His learning and conduct were lofty and ancient, and his reputation was preeminent throughout the two provinces of Zhejiang.

He specialized in the practice of Pure Land and frequently observed the Bhadrakalpika Samādhi (Banzhou Sanmei), remaining awake for ninety days and nights without sleep until the skin on his feet cracked and he vomited blood.

He did not cease his practice. In a dream, he saw Avalokiteśvara point to his mouth with a finger and pour nectar (*amṛta*) into it. Upon waking, his body and mind were refreshed and cool, and his illness was immediately cured.

He composed the *Jingtu jueyi xingyuan* (Resolving Doubts about the Pure Land through Practice and Vows) and the *Jingtu chanfa* (Pure Land Repentance Method), both of which circulated throughout the world.

On the day of his passing, he applied incense, prostrated before the Buddha, and made a vow to be reborn in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (*Sukhāvatī*). That evening, he sat upright and passed away; people saw a great star fall from the sky onto his spirit-shrine.
Jiufeng. Chan Master Ben of Yuanzhao (Song Zongben).
A native of Wuxi, Changzhou. Initially, he studied under Chan Master Tianyi Huai; through the practice of nianfo, he attained realization. Later...

He was transferred to Jingci Monastery and entered the Eastern Capital by imperial decree; his audience with the Emperor met with the Sovereign’s approval. In his daily life, he privately cultivated the practices of Pure Land Buddhism.

When the Dharma Master of Leifeng visited the Pure Land in a spiritual journey, he beheld a flower of extraordinary beauty. Upon being questioned, [the deity] replied, "It awaits Chan Master Ben of Jingci.
Furthermore, the Venerable Xi of Zifu came to pay homage at his feet and offered him gold. When asked the reason for this, he said, "In my meditative state, I saw gold."
He saw lotus flowers; these were those awaiting Master Ben. He further saw countless lotus flowers, some of which were withered within.
[The Master] said, "These are people who have fallen back. He then asked Master Ben, "Since you have devoted yourself to the study of Chan, why do you designate Pure Land as your practice?

He replied, "Although I am within the school of the Dharma-gate, I also cultivate Pure Land concurrently. Later, when his end approached, he passed away sitting upright. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Yuanzhao.

Master Jiu Fahua (also known as Song Kejiu) resided in Mingzhou. He constantly recited the Lotus Sūtra and vowed to be reborn in the Pure Land; thus, he was popularly known as Jiu Fahua. During the Tianjian era...
In the eighth year of the Yuanshou era, at the age of eighty-one, he passed away while seated in meditation. Three days later, he revived and said to others:
"I have seen the realm of the Pure Land, which accords perfectly with what is described in the sutras. Upon the lotus pedestals, the names of those destined to be reborn there were all inscribed.
I saw a golden pedestal marked with the name of Master Xun of Guangjiao Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture; another was marked for Sun Shierlang of Mingzhou; and another—"
The markers were long-lasting. At one silver terrace, she identified Mingzhou’s Daoist Nun Xu; having finished speaking, she transformed again.

Five years later, Daoist Nun Xu passed away, and a wondrous fragrance filled her chamber. Twelve years later, Sun Shierlang passed away, and celestial music welcomed him into the void—all exactly as she had said.
The name "Lotus" (Lianhua) serves as his designation; some may doubt that it is too ostentatious.
However, having spoken of his passing and subsequent resurrection, he further provided all these predictions several years in advance—how could such things not be worthy of belief?

The Great Master Jieliu (Cutter of the Stream) was named Xingce. He was the eighth son of Minister of Agriculture Jiang of Yixing during the late Ming dynasty. His father was Mr. Luchang. One night, Mr.
Luchang dreamed that the Great Master Hanshan entered his bedchamber; shortly thereafter, he was informed that Lady Yang had given birth to a son, who was the Master. At the age of... [text ends]
18. After his father passed away and the funeral rites were completed, he immediately went forth into the monastic life under Master Ruoyan of Wulin.

Later, at the invitation of Puren Monastery on Mount Yushan, he propagated the Dharma-gate of Pure Land. He practiced the recitation of the Buddha’s name six times daily, personally vowing to chant ten thousand recitations each time;

even during periods of great busyness, he never failed in this practice. He once composed the *Lianzang yiji* (A Collection from the Lotus Treasury) to exhort both the clergy and the laity. In the tenth year of the Kangxi era...
On the ninth day of the seventh month in the ninth year, he passed away while seated in meditation.

At the very moment of his passing, a young boy from a distant village was eating his midday meal when he suddenly dropped his chopsticks and fell to the ground; it took half a day for him to recover. When questioned, he said, "At this moment, Master Jieliu has attained rebirth.
The local deity commanded me to carry the banner to escort him. Furthermore, there was a man surnamed Wu from south of the city who had already died.
After several days, [the deity] suddenly spoke through a young child of the family, saying that he had personally witnessed the King of the Netherworld kneeling to see him off.
On that day, the courts of the netherworld suspended all executions for one day.

Regarding the Nuns’ Class for Rebirth in the Pure Land, the *Nidaming* (Great Illumination of Nuns) was compiled by the nun Nidaming of the Sui dynasty. Whenever entering the chamber to perform ritual recitation, one first dons clean robes and holds agarwood in the mouth. [This was done by] the Empress Dowager of Emperor Wen.

He held him in the highest esteem. On the day he was about to pass away, the assembly heard the fragrance of agarwood fill the chamber; shortly thereafter, a radiance like clouds appeared, which gradually faded toward the west and vanished.

The nun Jingzhen of Tang lived at Jixian Temple in Chang’an. Wearing patched robes and begging for alms, she recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* one hundred thousand times and single-mindedly recited the Buddha’s name.
She told her disciples: "Within five months, I have seen the Buddha ten times; twice I have seen the Jewel."

"The Child Playing upon the Lotus has already attained birth in the highest grade. Having spoken these words, she passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture, and auspicious light filled the hermitage.
Thus did the nun Wuxing attain enlightenment.
Tang Ni was a person of great intelligence who lived on Mount Lu reciting the Buddha’s name with a sincere vow to be reborn in the Pure Land.
Suddenly, he heard the sound of celestial music in the air and said to those around him, "I have already attained rebirth in the Middle Grade.
I see that for all my fellow practitioners who have recited the Buddha’s name with diligence, lotus flowers await them. Each of you must exert yourselves. Having spoken these words, he passed away.

Ninengfeng (also known as Nengfeng) was a native of Qiantang. She specialized in the cultivation of Pure Land practices. She once dreamed that the Buddha’s light illuminated her body and heard kind words from the air offering her consolation.
She told her disciples, "The time for my rebirth in the Pure Land has arrived. A short while later, she heard the sound of "Nianfo" (Buddha-recitation).

The sound was extremely intense. Upon looking at her, she was found sitting facing west with palms joined, having passed away. A strange fragrance filled the room, and the sound of music drifted toward the west.
This was the nun Fazang.
The Song dynasty nun Fazang resided in Jinling. She was diligent in her resolve to practice mindfulness of the Buddha and did not attend to external affairs.
One night, she saw Buddhas and Bodhisattvas arrive, their radiance shining brilliantly. With palms joined in mindfulness of the Buddha, she passed away.
Master Tiantai said: "The Buddha permitted his maternal aunt to leave the household life and lamented that the True Dharma would thereby decline.
Had it been as with the aforementioned five women who left the household life, would not the True Dharma have flourished all the more?
Yet, circumstances rendered this impossible; thus, the Buddha’s prophetic prediction was not in error."
The king and his ministers were reborn in the kingdom of Liu-yüan (Lūka).
The King of Liu-yüan, in the leisure moments between the myriad affairs of state, was deeply fond of the Buddha-dharma. He once said to his attendants: "I am the ruler of this nation..."
"Your Majesty, though you enjoy blessings and pleasures, you cannot escape impermanence. I have heard that the land of Amitābha Buddha in the West is a place where one may rest the spirit;
I shall now make a vow to seek rebirth in that realm. Thereupon, he practiced the Way and meditated on the Buddha during the six periods of the day.

Whenever making offerings to the Buddha or providing meals for the Sangha, the King and his consort personally served the food. This they did without ceasing for thirty years. At the time of his death, his countenance remained serene and joyful.
Yue and his companions all saw a transformation Buddha come to welcome them; the auspicious signs were manifold.

The Prince of Song, the Prince of Wei, and their father—these three men—and a Princess of the Imperial House were all practicing the path to the Western Paradise, yet only the wife did not practice it.

Later, the young lady died prematurely. Seven days after her death, she was restored to life and said to her mother, "I saw my father and my elder brother upon a pond of seven treasures in the western direction;
all three of us had lotus flowers. We shall later be reborn there, but you alone, Mother, have none."
"Therefore, I have returned briefly to inform you. I pray that you, Mother, will practice mindfulness of the Buddha as soon as possible. Having spoken these words, he closed his eyes and passed away.

From this, his mother immediately gave rise to faith and practiced mindfulness of the Buddha without weariness. Subsequently, they passed away one after another through seated meditation, each manifesting auspicious signs at the time of death.

Liu Yimin, General of the Interior (Canjun) during the Jin dynasty. A native of Pengcheng, he was a descendant of Chu Yuanwang. Orphaned at a young age, he became renowned for his filial piety toward his mother.

He initially served as a General of the Interior for the provincial administration but then withdrew into seclusion. Although both Xie An and Liu Yu recommended him repeatedly, he did not accept their offers. He entered Mount Lu and joined the community of Huiyuan.

The Duke established a Lotus Society (*padmavāṭī*) and devoted himself single-mindedly to the practice of *nien-fo* (Buddha-recitation). After practicing for a long time without slackening, he frequently saw, within his meditative concentration, the light of the Buddha illuminating the ground, all of which turned the color of gold.
After fifteen years, he beheld Amitābha Buddha’s light from the white tuft between his eyebrows (*ūrṇā-kośa*) shining forth, as the Buddha lowered his hand to comfort and welcome him.
Liu prostrated himself and pleaded earnestly, saying, "How may the Tathāgata’s hand touch my head and his robe cover my body? Suddenly, the Buddha—
He comforted her with these words. One night, he again dreamed that the Tathāgata had a halo around his neck and the *svastika* on his chest;
the Buddha pointed to the water of eight virtues in a pond and ordered him to drink it. Liu drank it and found it sweet and delicious. Upon waking, a wondrous fragrance emanated from his pores.
He then addressed the assembly, saying, "The conditions for rebirth in the Pure Land have arrived. He burned incense before the image and made this vow: "By means of Śākyamuni..."

In accordance with the Tathāgata’s bequeathed teachings, knowing that there is Amitābha Buddha, he first offered incense to Śākyamuni Tathāgata, followed by offerings to Amitābha Buddha and the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, making this aspiration:
"May all sentient beings be born together in the Pure Land. Having spoken these words, he finished.
He joined his palms, faced west, and passed away.

Ma Ziyun, the District Magistrate of Tang, was a candidate for the "Filial and Incorrupt" (Xiaolian) examination. Serving as the District Magistrate of Jing, he was transporting grain-tax revenue to the capital when his boat encountered a storm and sank. He was...

He was imprisoned and devoted himself single-mindedly to the recitation of the Buddha’s name for five years. Upon encountering a general amnesty, he entered Nanling Mountain Temple to live in seclusion.

One day he said to others, "Throughout my life I have practiced the recitation of the Buddha’s name with diligent devotion; now that my pure karma is perfected, I am about to attain rebirth in the Pure Land.

The next day, after bathing and adjusting his robes, he sat upright with palms joined. A wondrous fragrance filled the room, and he said joyfully, "The Buddha has come to welcome me. He spoke thus and passed away.
Shortly thereafter, he passed away.

Zhang Di, the Assistant Instructor (Jiàozhū) from Song, was a native of Qiantang who served as an Assistant Instructor in office. He received the Bodhisattva precepts from Vinaya Master Yuanjing and sought his instruction.
Regarding the Dharma-gate of Purifying Karma, he practiced it with sincere resolve, vowing to be reborn in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (An-yang).

Whenever he practiced mindfulness of the Buddha, he recited with such vigor and raised his voice so loudly that he continued even until his voice failed. One day, he said to Yuanjing, "In samādhi, I saw white kalaviṅka birds."
He performed aerial dances before [the image]. After another three years, he sat upright facing west, recited the Buddha’s name, and passed away.

Song Wang Rixiu, a Jinshi of Longshu, was a native of Longshu. He was dignified, serene, simple, and pure, having read extensively through the classics and histories; yet one day, he cast them all aside and said:
"These are all merely records of karma; they are not the ultimate Dharma. I shall take Western Paradise as my destination. From then on, he practiced the recollection of the Buddha with diligence.
At the age of sixty, he wore simple cloth garments and subsisted on vegetarian food. He performed a thousand prostrations daily, sleeping only at the second watch of the night.

He composed a "Treatise on the Pure Land" to exhort the world. Three days before his passing, he took leave of all his acquaintances. On the appointed day, after finishing his reading, he performed his usual rites of recollection.
Suddenly, he called out "Amitābha Buddha" in a stern voice and proclaimed, "The Buddha comes to welcome me. He stood upright and passed away.
Local people dreamed of two youths leading the Master westward; consequently, every household painted his image and worshipped it as if it were a deity.

Daifu Ge Fan of Song was a native of Chengjiang. Having passed the imperial examinations in his youth, he rose to the rank of Chao-san. Whether in public offices or private residences, he invariably established a pure chamber and installed Buddha images.
Once, while entering the room to perform ritual recitations, śarīra relics descended from the sky. In his daily life, he...

He purified his karma and universally exhorted both monastics and laypeople; many were moved by his transformation. Once, while in meditative absorption, a monk traveled spiritually to the Pure Land and saw Fan there.
Subsequently, Fan passed away without illness, sitting upright facing west.

Yang Wuweī (楊無為), the Judicial Intendant, was surnamed Yang Jie (楊傑). A native of Wuweī Prefecture, he was styled Wuweīzi (無為子). Having passed the imperial examinations in his youth, he served as the Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

He later held the office of Judicial Intendant for the Two Zhejiang Circuits. He revered the Buddha-dharma and attained clear realization of the Chan school, asserting that the faculties of sentient beings possess [the potential for awakening].
Whether of sharp or dull faculties, it is easy to understand and easy to practice; there is only the Western Pure Land.

He composed the preface to the *Ten Doubts on the Pure Land* (*Tiantai Shiyi Lun*) and the preface to the *Collection for Resolving Doubts about the Pure Land* (*Jingtu Jueyi Ji*), propagating the dharma-gate of practicing for rebirth in the Pure Land. In his later years, he painted an image of Maitreya Buddha sixteen feet tall.
He followed this practice with offerings, which moved the Buddha to come and welcome him; he passed away while sitting upright.

Wen Yanbo, Duke Lu of Song—Wen Yanbo deeply revered the Triple Gem and devoted himself exclusively to the cultivation of Pure Land practices. While residing in the capital, he [associated] with the Dharma Master Jingyan...

The Master established a society for the recitation of the Buddha’s name, once encouraging as many as one hundred thousand people. At that time, a scholar-official composed a verse for him which said:
“I know your courage is as vast as heaven; I pray you will form the karmic bond with a hundred thousand in the West.

Not seeking a livelihood for yourself alone, Let us all board together the boat that ferries beings across. When his end approached, he was free from illness; he passed away peacefully while reciting the Buddha’s name.

Zhongli Shaoshi was Zhongli Jin of the Song dynasty. While serving as the Judicial Commissioner of Zhexi, he encountered the Master of Repentance Ciyun and consequently developed a profound faith in the Pure Land.

Later, when he served as the Prefect of Kaifeng, he exhausted himself in state affairs when out, but upon returning home, he would remain sleepless reciting the Buddha’s name. One night, he suddenly summoned his family members.
He rose, requested a bath, changed his clothes, and passed away while seated. The entire family saw that Jing was riding upon a blue lotus flower, being welcomed and led westward by celestial music.
Qian Xiangzu, the Prefectural Governor, [recorded this].
Qian Xiangzu of the Song dynasty, whose style name was Zhian, while serving as the governor of Jinling, never ceased reciting the Buddha’s name outside of his official duties.
He frequently established over ten guesthouses and monasteries in his native region, all of which he named after Pure Land and Sukhāvatī.

After the Left Minister resigned and returned home, he devoted himself even more single-mindedly to the practice of pure karma (*śukla-karma*). In the second month of the fourth year of the Jiading era, he suffered from a slight illness.

He requested a brush and wrote a verse, then passed away while sitting in the lotus posture. Later, someone dreamed that the Master had been reborn in the Western Paradise as the Bodhisattva Maitreya (Ciji).

The Imperial Censor Wang Minzhong, whose courtesy name was Minzhong, served as the Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites during the Song dynasty. Compassionate and benevolent toward all living beings, his family had abstained from killing for seven generations.

He was deeply attuned to the Chan school and further devoted his mind to the Pure Land, authoring the *Direct Pointing to the Pure Land: A Collection for Resolving Doubts* in three volumes to universally exhort others.

He practiced mindfulness of the Buddha; whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, he made the contemplation of mindfulness of the Buddha his sole concern. His rosary was never out of his hand.
Later, while sitting in meditation and reciting the Buddha’s name, he bathed, changed his clothes, and passed away.
There was a monk whose spirit traveled to the Pure Land, where he saw Gu and Ge Fan together; this provides further evidence that rebirth there is indeed possible.
As for the layman’s rebirth, it is comparable to that of Zhou Xuzhi.
Zhou Xuzhi of the Jin dynasty was a native of Yanmen. At the age of twelve, he had mastered the Five Classics and the Five *Wei*, earning him the title "The Boy of the Ten Classics.

Although high officials repeatedly invited him to serve, he declined them all. He attended upon Master Huiyuan of Mount Lu and joined the Lotus Society. When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he summoned him for an audience and engaged him in debate;

the Emperor was greatly pleased. He was then known as "Master Tongyin" (the Recluse of Profundity). Later, he resided on Mount Zhong, where he devoted himself single-mindedly to the recitation of the Buddha’s name.
As he grew older, his devotion became increasingly steadfast. One day, facing the sky, he said, "The Buddha has come to welcome me," and with palms joined, he passed away.

Song Man (also known as Sui Songman) was a native of Changzhou. He would count his beans while reciting the Buddha’s name, accumulating a total of thirty *shí*. In the ninth month of the eighth year of the Kaihuang era, he passed away.

After finishing his meal for the monastic community, he sat down and passed away. People saw celestial flowers and extraordinary fragrances filling the air as he ascended into the void and departed toward the west.

Zheng Muqing of Tang devoted his entire family to the recitation of the Buddha’s name. During the Kaiyuan era, when he was gravely ill, someone urged him to consume fish and meat; he remained firm [in his refusal].
He did not grant permission. Holding a censer in his hand, he vowed to seek rebirth in the Pure Land. Suddenly, a wondrous fragrance filled the air, and he passed away in silence.
Su Ting, the Minister of the Interior, was his maternal uncle; in a dream, he saw a precious lotus pond bloom, and the Prefectural Governor sitting upon it.
Yuanci (Tang Yuanci) resided at Guanyin Temple in Runzhou. He recited the *Amitābha Sūtra* and practiced mindfulness of the Buddha.

Suddenly, he fell slightly ill and smelled a fragrance from the air accompanied by the sound of music. It seemed as though someone said: "The coarse music has passed; the subtle music follows. You shall..."
He departed, passing away while reciting the name of the Buddha. A rare fragrance did not dissipate for several days.
Sūn Liángsòng, a native of Qiántáng, lived in seclusion and studied the *Tripitaka*, attaining a profound mastery of the essential principles of the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*. He relied upon Dàzhì...
The Vinaya Master had received the Bodhisattva precepts and recited the Buddha’s name ten thousand times daily for twenty years without ceasing.

Suddenly, he instructed his family to invite monks to recite the Buddha’s name to assist him in his rebirth. When the monks had assembled and had been reciting for only half a session, he joined his palms toward the sky and said:
The Buddha and the Bodhisattvas have already graced us with their descent and now depart, sitting back and passing into transformation.

Wang Tian, known as Song Wangtian, was a native of Siming. He styled himself the "Old Man of No Merit. Regarding the fundamental tenets of all Chan monasteries and the teachings of the Tiantai school, there was none [he did not master].

He did not achieve thorough penetration [of the Dharma]. He authored the *Jingtu zixin lu* (Record of Self-Confidence in the Pure Land). In his later years, he devoted himself single-mindedly to the recitation of the Buddha’s name.
He passed away while seated facing west; a wondrous fragrance was rich and pervasive. When his coffin was cremated, one hundred and eight śarīras, as large as soybeans, were obtained.

Sun Zhong of the Song dynasty was a native of Siming. From an early age, he admired the Western Paradise and built a hermitage where he practiced mindfulness of the Buddha. Later, falling ill, he invited one hundred monks to recite the Buddha’s name for him.
Suddenly, he raised his hands in homage toward the sky, forming two mudrās with his fingers, and passed away with a serene expression. The entire city heard the sound of celestial music.
Delighting in various fragrances, he gradually sank toward the west. His two sons also focused their minds single-mindedly on the Buddha and passed away while seated in succession.

Shen Quan of the Song dynasty was from Qiantang; together with his wife, Shi, he devoted himself exclusively to the practice of the Pure Land. All his ordinary good deeds were utilized for this purpose.

He dedicated his merits. Later, he and his wife passed away one after the other; both were met by the arrival of a transformation Buddha, accompanied by the auspicious omen of celestial music reaching their ears.
— Recorded by Tang Shiliang.
Song Tang Shiliang was a native of Kuaiji. He observed the precepts and recited the name of the Buddha, chanting the *Amitābha Sūtra* one hundred thousand times.
One day he suddenly said, "The Buddha has come to welcome me. Having finished speaking, he prostrated himself and immediately passed away. Someone was present at Daowei Mountain.
In a dream, he saw a wondrous light to the west, with banners, flowers, and celestial music. A voice from the air proclaimed: "Tang Shiliang has already returned to the Pure Land.

Lu Jun (also known as Song Lu Jun) was a native of Qiantang. In his youth, he served in government offices, but after a long time, he abandoned them to devote himself to the practice of the Pure Land. Every...
He repented before the Buddha, tears streaming down to his chin. At the time of his death, he invited Vinaya Master Yuanjing to instruct him on the Western Paradise.
As they recited the *Amitābha Sūtra* up to the section on the Highest Grade, Yuanjing said, "You may go. Zunjing replied, "The assembly of holy ones has not yet gathered; let us wait for a moment."
After a short while, he suddenly rose and went to his bamboo bed; facing west, he sat upright and passed away.
Wu Zizhang Yuan was a native of Suzhou whose family had practiced medicine for generations. Together with his elder brother’s son, Zicai, he studied under Master Yunwu.

He was diligent in the mindfulness of the Buddha, and his entire family followed the Dharma. During the Zhizheng era, he passed away peacefully without illness, with his palms joined as he recited the Buddha’s name.
He was the Grand Marshal (Taigong) of the Lotus Society.
Regarding Ming Lianhua Taigong: he was a man of Yue who throughout his life was simple and unadorned. He did nothing but recite the Buddha’s name day and night without ceasing.

After his death, a single lotus flower suddenly grew upon his coffin. His relatives were filled with wonder and marvel, and from this they knew that he would certainly attain rebirth in the Pure Land.
The layman Hua Minghua was a native of Jianggan. He was pure, simple, and free of artifice; he knew nothing other than seeking rebirth in the Western Pure Land.

In his middle years, he entrusted his family estate to his son and lived alone in a single room, withdrawing from worldly affairs. Morning and evening, he applied himself with tireless diligence to the recitation of the Buddha’s name. Later, he was about to...
He passed away. Knowing that the time had come, he changed his clothes, adjusted his cap, took leave of the assembly, and departed.

Among his family was Wu Mao, a member of the Wu Liufang household of Qingyang, a lay practitioner of the Wu clan. He observed the precepts, cultivated goodness, and recited the Buddha’s name without ceasing during the Shunzhi era.

In the first year, coinciding with the crossing of the Yangtze River by the troops of the Left [faction], the entire family fled to take refuge. Wu Mao alone remained behind to guard the residence, where he was struck by seven spear thrusts from bandits and died.
A short while later, his younger brother came to look for him; he had already revived and said, "I have karmic debts from past lives that would have required me to undergo seven births as a pig.
By the power of my fasting and precepts, I have dispersed the resentment of those seven spear thrusts. From this point on, I shall go straight to the Western [Pure Land]."
It was indeed so. Later, his master saw, in a state of trance, a divine being in the expanse of the sky, with banners and streamers before and behind, of incomparable majesty.
The being called out and said, "I am Maoyi of Wu; having reached the celestial realm, I happened to pass by here.
Having finished speaking, he vanished. The master then painted his likeness and paid him reverent homage.
Zhou Yisheng, Zhou Yisheng.
He was a member of the Kunshan gentry who resided at Houshiqiao. He practiced medicine and did not calculate profit with the poor;

whenever a patient summoned him, he would go immediately. During the day, he recited the Buddha’s name without ceasing, single-mindedly seeking rebirth in the Western Paradise. He passed away peacefully.
During the Xi-yi-si period, when he was already seventy years of age, he suddenly desired to depart this world. He said to his family members, "Bring me pen and inkstone;
I wish to write a verse before I go. Having finished writing, he then peacefully recited the Buddha's name and passed away.
Shen Chengxian of Kunshan.
He resided in Xuanhuafang and made his living as a carpenter. Over seventy years of age, he observed the fasts and recited the Buddha’s name, single-mindedly cultivating the Pure Land.
His hands never ceased from wielding the axe, yet the sound of the Buddha’s name never left his mouth. (Kangxi...)

In the third month of the tenth year, he knew in advance that the time had come. Three days prior, he took leave of his relatives and fellow practitioners, saying, "I am about to be reborn in the Western Pure Land;
henceforth, we shall not meet again. He told his son’s daughter-in-law, "Tomorrow is the fifteenth; I shall attain rebirth then.
The following morning, after bathing and changing his robes, he sat upright facing west. Taking a clean basin and placing it before him, he leaned upon it...
He then recited the Buddha’s name, burned incense, sat in the lotus posture, and passed away.

Wang Menglin, whose courtesy name was also Wang Menglin, was a son of the Confucian tradition from Kunshan. Throughout his life, he taught students; he was sincere and free of hypocrisy. He had one son.
His style name was Xiāngchén. He was exceptionally filial toward his parents. During the day, he devoted himself solely to the practice of *nienfo* (reciting the Buddha’s name).

In the forty-first year of the Kāngxī era, when he was already over seventy years old, he suffered from a slight illness in early winter. On the first ten days of the eleventh month, I went to inquire after him.
Mènglín said, "The seventeenth [of this month] is what the world calls the birthday of Amitābha. On that day, I performed [the rites].
I said, "When the appointed time arrives, I shall come to see you off. On the seventeenth day, I went to visit him early in the morning;
although he was bedridden with illness, his countenance remained serene. I said, "Master, you must resolve to attain Bodhicitta.

Quoting from the sutras, I said, "If one practices without resolving to attain Bodhicitta, it is like tilling a field without sowing seeds. Thereupon, I discussed the Four Great Vows with him in detail.
Menglin nodded in agreement. I said, "I shall take my leave for a short while and return later," and then secretly instructed his son, Xiangchen:
"If your father should pass away, do not call out or weep. When I went back after the meal, Menglin had already passed away through the practice of mindfulness of the Buddha.

Among the Menglin clan, there was one named Zhen-sheng, who was my relative by marriage. His father, Yan-fu, was a good friend of mine at the Kunshan Academy and was a devoted follower of the Triple Gem.
Zhen-sheng was a handsome youth, skilled in calligraphy, but possessed many worldly habits and did not place much faith in the teachings.
One day he fell ill and saw a large black ghost; he believed this to be an enemy from a previous life. Zhen-sheng...

He was deeply terrified. He then courageously and fervently recited the Buddha’s name, seeking rebirth in the Western Land. When his recitation of the Buddha’s name slackened slightly, the ghostly form reappeared.
Consequently, his aspiration for rebirth became even more urgent and his recitation of the Buddha’s name grew even sharper. After several days of such recitation, the ghost no longer appeared.

The Biography of the Layman Shenglian.
The layman Shenglian was Luo Ziyunmei of Loudong. His original style name was Layman Wupian (The Unbiased). Why [was he called Shenglian]?
He was also called Shenglian. In the autumn of the fortieth year of the Kangxi era, Yunmei fell ill and his condition grew critical;

he intended to compose a verse to bid farewell to this world when he suddenly heard a voice from the air say: "Layman Shenglian, you still have ten years of life remaining; you need not compose this verse."
From this point on, he recovered completely; his relatives were all amazed by this. For this reason, everyone gave him the name Layman Shenglian.
